title: Learned-manipulation robot makers land two customer-co-led rounds by H1 2027
body: Walden Robotics' $300 million seed at a $1.1 billion valuation is notable less for its size than for its sequencing: the robots were already doing production work at a Toyota plant in North America since February 2026, having gone from first pilot to real production tasks in under two months, and Toyota then co-led the round for a company it was already a customer of, with Boeing, Samsung Ventures and Prologis Ventures joining the cap table. That is a vendor underwritten by its prospective buyers on the evidence of a running deployment rather than by a financial thesis about humanoids. The technical precondition is what makes that sequencing possible: Large Behavior Models paired with Diffusion Policy let a machine acquire a task through real-world practice instead of hand-scripted motion, which collapses the integration work that historically kept factory automation on multi-year schedules and made in-plant proof-of-value impossible to show before a raise. Once a two-month pilot-to-production window is demonstrably achievable, the underwriting standard moves with it — an industrial buyer that can run the pilot cheaply holds both the information advantage and the incentive to take equity before a competitor does. By H1 2027, expect at least two more general-purpose robotics companies to close rounds of $100 million or more in which an industrial operator — a manufacturer, aerospace prime or logistics operator rather than a financial fund — is lead or co-lead, and in which the announcement names a deployment already performing production work rather than a pilot yet to begin. The falsifiable element is that conjunction: strategic participation in robotics megarounds is already routine, while a named live deployment disclosed at the raise is not.

reasoning.because: Walden's robots ran production work in a Toyota plant since February, months before its $300M seed
reasoning.given: Learned manipulation cuts pilot-to-production to two months, giving buyers evidence funds lack
reasoning.so_that: ≥2 more robotics vendors close $100M+ rounds led or co-led by an industrial operator with a live deployment named
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027; ≥2 operator-co-led $100M+ robotics rounds naming live deployments
reasoning.plain_language: A robot startup got funded because its robots were already working in a Toyota factory — expect other factories to invest the same way.

summary: Walden Robotics raised $300M at $1.1B with Toyota co-leading, after its robots were already doing production work in a Toyota plant. Learned manipulation cut pilot-to-production to two months, so buyers can underwrite on evidence. Expect two more operator-co-led $100M+ rounds by H1 2027.
